status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Structural shape: chapters 1-43 are almost entirely sustained wisdom/ethical instruction in the voice of the author ("My son..."), not narrative - grouped into 10 law/theme tiers by topic cluster, all deliveredBy the author (Jesus son of Sirach) except the "Wisdom's Self-Praise" tier (ch.24), which is explicitly voiced in the first person BY Wisdom herself, not by Sirach - deliveredBy left null there since Wisdom-personified is a literary figure, not a human manager. Chapters 44-52 ("Let us now praise famous men") are a compressed biographical catalogue of the whole OT canon from Adam to Nehemiah, giving real (if often brief) person-tiers - this is the book's one genuinely narrative/historical section and the natural home for most of its manager roster. The author closes the book by naming himself explicitly (50:27, "I Jesus, the son of Sirach Eleazar, of Jerusalem") and then gives his own first-person testimony of a near-death deliverance and lifelong pursuit of wisdom - personally embodied, not transmission-only, so he gets his own Person tier rather than being folded into the law tiers he delivers everything else through. REAL DATA-QUALITY ISSUE FOUND IN THIS FILE, flagged per project rule rather than silently fixed: chapter 51 in this JSON is a verbatim duplicate of chapter 50 (the entire Simon-the-high-priest passage repeats word-for-word), and the text that is traditionally chapter 51 of Ecclesiasticus (Sirach's own autobiographical thanksgiving/wisdom-quest poem) is instead labeled chapter 52 here - an apparent off-by-one mislabeling during extraction, not a genuine content difference. Verse references below cite the file's actual (mislabeled) chapter numbers as they exist in ecclesiasticus_46.json today, so they resolve correctly against the live data; if the extraction is ever corrected, these two chapter numbers will need to shift down by one. NAMING COLLISION explicitly flagged, not merged: two different men named Jesus appear in this book - the author "Jesus, the son of Sirach Eleazar" (50:27, 52) and "Jesus the son of Josedek" the co-builder of the Second Temple alongside Zerubbabel (49:12) - kept as fully separate characters, ids suffixed distinctly. Genealogy fields are left null throughout except where this text itself states a lineage (e.g. "son of Nun" for Joshua, "son of Jesse" for David, "son of Onias" for Simon) - Ecclesiasticus is a praise-catalogue, not a genealogical record, and does not restate most figures' parentage; fuller genealogy for these same figures lives in their own books' Character Index entries (Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Samuel, Kings, etc.) and was not re-derived here to avoid inventing beyond what this text actually says. Undifferentiated group per rule 5: "the twelve prophets" (49:10) are given one collective entry rather than twelve invented individuals, since the text itself only ever refers to them collectively. Chapters 28-32, 34-37, 41-43 were confirmed present and topically consistent with the surrounding wisdom-instruction chapters via direct read but are represented through the same 10 topic-cluster law tiers rather than being split further, since none introduced content-distinct enough (a new named figure or a genuinely separate teaching subject) to warrant an 11th tier on its own.

scribeTiers.scribeName: The Praise of Craftsmen and the Scribe

characters.name: Jesus, son of Sirach Eleazar (the author)

verses.note: Names himself as the author: 'I have written in this book the instruction of understanding and knowledge, I Jesus, the son of Sirach Eleazar, of Jerusalem, who out of his heart poured forth wisdom.'
First-person thanksgiving: recounts being delivered from slander, false accusation, and near-death peril, and praises the Lord as his protector.
Recounts his own lifelong personal pursuit of Wisdom from his youth, 'from my youth I tracked her out,' and gives thanks for the wisdom he attained.
Closes the book inviting the unlearned to come and receive instruction 'without money.'

funFacts: Is the one named human author of an entire book in this Character Index project so far - the whole text is explicitly framed as his personal instruction to 'my son,' making every law/theme tier in this book his own delivered teaching.

characters.name: Wisdom (personified)
characters.purpose: Wisdom herself speaks in the first person, recounting that she came forth from the mouth of the Most High before all creation, sought a resting place among every people, and was given her dwelling specifically in Israel and in the Law of Moses - a distinct hymn voiced by Wisdom, not by the author.

verses.note: 'I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a mist.'
The Creator commands her tabernacle to rest specifically 'in Jacob... in Israel.'
Identifies herself with 'the law which Moses commanded us for a heritage.'
'The Lord created man of the earth, and turned him back unto it again.'
'And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.'
'A heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam' - his name used as the general term for mankind bearing the burden of mortality.
'Above every living thing in the creation is Adam' - final summary line of the Praise of the Fathers catalogue.
Paired with Seth: 'Shem and Seth were glorified among men' - no distinguishing action given in this text.
Paired with Shem: 'Shem and Seth were glorified among men' - no distinguishing action given in this text.
'Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, being an example of repentance to all generations.'
'No man was created upon the earth such as was Enoch; for he was taken up from the earth.'
'Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the season of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world.'
'Everlasting covenants were made with him, that all flesh should no more be blotted out by a flood.'
'Abraham was a great father of a multitude of nations; and there was none found like him in glory.'
Kept the law of the Most High and was found faithful when proved - a reference to his circumcision covenant.
Sworn oath that his seed would be multiplied as the dust of the earth and the stars, and given the land 'from sea to sea.'
'In Isaac also did he establish likewise, for Abraham his father's sake, the blessing of all men, and the covenant.'

characters.name: Jacob

verses.note: The covenant rests upon his head; his inheritance divided among twelve tribes.

funFacts: 'Jacob'/'the heritage of Jacob' is also used dozens of times throughout the wisdom-instruction chapters (e.g. 23:12, 24:8) as a poetic stand-in for Israel as a whole, not as further narrative about Jacob personally.

verses.note: 'A man beloved of God and men, even Moses, whose memorial is blessed.'
Given commandments face to face, led into the thick darkness, given 'the law of life and knowledge' to teach Jacob.
Consecrates and anoints Aaron with holy oil for the everlasting priesthood.
Dathan, Abiram, and the congregation of Korah rise against him in the wilderness and are destroyed by the Lord's wrath.
'He exalted Aaron, a holy man like unto him, even his brother, of the tribe of Levi.'
Given the everlasting priestly covenant and described at length in his priestly vestments - ephod, breastplate with Urim and Thummim, gold mitre inscribed HOLINESS.
Given the firstfruits of the people's increase as his priestly portion, since 'he himself is thy portion and inheritance.'
'Third in glory' after Moses and Aaron, 'in that he was zealous in the fear of the Lord... and he made reconciliation for Israel' when the people turned away.
Granted a covenant of peace, that he and his seed should hold the dignity of the priesthood for ever.
'Valiant in war, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies... that he might give Israel their inheritance.'
'Did not the sun go back by his hand? And did not one day become as two?' - the long-day miracle.
With Caleb, withstood the adversary and stilled the murmuring of wickedness in the time of Moses.
Alongside Joshua, one of only two of the six hundred thousand preserved to enter the land; the Lord's strength remained with him unto his old age.
'The prophet of the Lord, beloved of his Lord, established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people.'
Before his death, protests before the Lord and his anointed that he never took so much as a shoe from any man.
Even after death, prophesies from the earth, showing the king his end.

genealogy.father: Jesse (stated in text, 47:1's tribe reference and 'son of Jesse' at 45:25)

verses.note: 'Played with lions as with kids... in his youth did he not slay a giant... when he lifted up his hand with a sling stone, and beat down the boasting of Goliath?'
Set singers before the altar and ordered the feast seasons in the sanctuary.
'The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever; and gave him a covenant of kings.'
A separate covenant made with David 'the son of Jesse, of the tribe of Judah,' that the kingship inherits son to son, paired directly with Aaron's priestly inheritance.
'After him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the days of David.'
'A son, a man of understanding... reigned in days of peace... that he might set up a house for his name.'
Praised for wisdom filling him 'as a river,' his songs, proverbs, and parables famed even to distant isles.
'Thou didst bow thy loins unto women... thou didst blemish thine honour' - his downfall through foreign wives, causing the kingdom's division.

characters.name: Rehoboam

verses.note: Left behind by Solomon as heir, described as 'the foolishness of the people, and one that lacked understanding, who made the people to revolt by his counsel.'

funFacts: Named alongside Jeroboam son of Nebat ('who made Israel to sin') as the two figures blamed for the kingdom's division - Jeroboam is not given his own submanager entry here since the text gives him no independent action beyond that single indictment line.

verses.note: 'Arose... as fire, and his word burned like a torch... by the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven: thrice did he thus bring down fire.'
'Who did raise up a dead man from death.'
'Who was taken up in a tempest of fire, in a chariot of fiery horses.'
'Elisha was filled with his spirit... nothing was too high for him; and when he was laid on sleep his body prophesied.'
The Lord 'delivered them by the hand of Isaiah' when Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem.
'Isaiah the prophet... was great and faithful in his vision.'
By his word the sun went backward for Hezekiah, and he foretold hidden things to come.
'Fortified his city, and brought in water into the midst of them: he digged the sheer rock with iron, and builded up wells for waters.'
Sennacherib and Rabshakeh come against him; the people are in anguish 'as women in travail.'
'Hezekiah did that which was pleasing to the Lord, and was strong in the ways of David his father.'
Named, with David and Josiah, as one of only three kings of Judah who did not commit trespass against the law.
'The memorial of Josiah is like the composition of incense... it shall be sweet as honey in every mouth.'
'He behaved himself uprightly in the conversion of the people, and took away the abominations of iniquity.'
Named, with David and Hezekiah, as one of only three kings of Judah who did not commit trespass against the law.
The burning of the city 'was written by the hand of Jeremiah.'
'He was sanctified in the womb to be a prophet, to root out, and to afflict, and to destroy; and in like manner to build and to plant.'
'It was Ezekiel who saw the vision of glory, which God shewed him upon the chariot of the cherubim.'

characters.name: The Twelve Prophets (collective)

verses.note: 'Also of the twelve prophets may the bones flourish again out of their place... and he comforted Jacob, and delivered them by confidence of hope.' Named only collectively - no individual minor prophet is distinguished by name in this text.

funFacts: Kept as one collective entry per the project's rule against inventing individuals for an undifferentiated named group - the text gives them no individual lines to divide.

verses.note: 'How shall we magnify Zerubbabel? And he was as a signet on the right hand.'

characters.name: Jesus, son of Josedek

verses.note: 'So was Jesus the son of Josedek: who in their days builded the house, and exalted a people holy to the Lord.' Co-builder of the Second Temple alongside Zerubbabel.

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION, deliberately not merged: this is a different 'Jesus' from the book's own author, Jesus son of Sirach - see book-level notes.

verses.note: 'Of Nehemiah the memorial is great; who raised up for us the walls that were fallen, and set up the gates and bars, and raised up our homes again.'
'Neither was there a man born like unto Joseph, a governor of his brethren, a stay of the people: yea, his bones were visited.'
'The great priest, who in his life repaired the house, and in his days strengthened the temple... built from the foundation the height of the double wall.'
Extended series of similes describing his glory when emerging from the sanctuary - as the morning star, the full moon, the sun, the rainbow, roses, lilies, an olive tree, a cypress.
Officiates the full sacrificial service at the altar, robed in glory, surrounded by 'all the sons of Aaron,' the trumpets sounded, and blesses the whole congregation.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk/unresolved references kept out of the character list - none of these are given independent action in this text and are not worth inventing individual entries for.

adversariesOfMoses.note: Dathan, Abiram, and the congregation of Korah rise against Moses and Aaron and are destroyed - named as antagonists, not managers/submanagers, since they oppose rather than support the tier's manager.

jeroboam.note: 'Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, and gave unto Ephraim a way of sin' - given one indictment line alongside Rehoboam, no independent action of his own in this text; not promoted to a submanager entry.

twoNationsAndAFoolishPeople.note: 'They that sit upon the mountain of Samaria, and the Philistines, and that foolish people that dwelleth in Sichem' - collective peoples the author's soul is vexed by, not individual characters.
